item.title: Get ready! These neighborhoods in Mazatlán will be without water on Monday, December 29th.
item.description: Approximately 20 neighborhoods in the port city of Mazatlán will be without drinking water service next Monday, December 29, the Municipal Water and Sewerage Board (JUMAPAM) announced. The agency stated that hydrant installation and maintenance will be carried out on that date, resulting in restricted water service for much of the day. item.title: More than 79,000 new tourists visited Mazatlán in 2025
item.description: Mazatlán, known as “The Pearl of the Pacific,” is one of Mexico’s top tourist destinations thanks to its picturesque scenery, gastronomy, culture, and more, attracting many new tourists. From October 2024 to October 2025, the Ministry of Tourism registered 79,000 new tourists in the port city. item.title: BreakingNews Reports indicate a sharp depreciation in the Sinaloa real estate market
item.description: The real estate market is experiencing a sharp decline in the state. In Culiacán, property values ​​have depreciated by up to 40%, primarily due to the context of violence, while in Mazatlán the drop is around 20%, also influenced by an oversupply of high-rise housing and a demand that hasn’t kept pace. item.title: In 2025, 715 sea turtle nests were rescued in Mazatlán.
item.description: During 2025, 715 sea turtle nests were rescued on Mazatlán’s beaches as part of a protection program operating along a 16-kilometer stretch of coastline. This stretch extends from Cerritos Beach to Olas Altas. item.description: During the Christmas and New Year’s celebrations, Sinaloa Civil Protection responded to a total of 19 incidents in various municipalities throughout the state, most of them related to traffic accidents and vehicles running off the road, reported the agency’s director, Roy Navarrete Cuevas.
